summary.intent: Execute Phase 59 (FUSE IPNS Verify/Publish Hardening and Cleanup) — 4 sequential plans addressing file key-wrap error propagation, VerifyError::Legacy enum enrichment, dead-code removal, and first-publish sequence unification across the cipherbox-fuse crate.
summary.outcome: Waves 1 and 2 (plans 59-01 and 59-02) completed and verified with 95 passing tests. Wave 3 (59-03) was running at transcript end. A parallel staging DB query to count legacy IPNS records was in-flight but results not yet shown.

repo: Root `npm test` is `pnpm --parallel -r run test` (full monorepo) — always scope post-merge gates to `cargo -p cipherbox-fuse` for Rust-only phases to avoid RAM starvation.

`VerifyError::Legacy` was a unit variant; migrated in 59-02 to carry `{ cid: String, sequence_number: String }` across 9 match-arm sites in 6 files, eliminating a redundant IPNS resolve round-trip and a ~1ms race window.
Legacy IPNS records are discriminated by `signed_record IS NULL` in the `folder_ipns` table — signing convention landed 2026-04-04 (PR #448) which added nullable `signed_record`/`public_key` columns.

Staging Postgres: container `cipherbox-staging-postgres-1`, user `cipherbox`, db `cipherbox_staging`. Nested quoting breaks inside `docker exec` — use stdin-piped psql (`docker exec -i ... psql ... <<< 'SQL'`).

TEE re-signs enrolled IPNS names every 6h, so any vault touched since 2026-04-04 has self-healed legacy rows. Surviving legacy records are only dormant names created in the ~1-month window before signing shipped.
winfsp and crypto-clippy build failures on macOS are pre-existing CI-only issues, not regressions — documented in 59-01 SUMMARY as known caveats.

code.finding: Finding A (59-01): `build_folder_metadata` was swallowing `wrap_key` errors and publishing a FilePointer with `ipns_private_key_encrypted: None`, making the file unrecoverable. Fixed to propagate the error.

Finding B (59-01): inode cache was not re-resolving when a file's `file_meta_ipns_name` pointer changed under an unchanged mtime, returning stale CID/keys. Fixed to force re-resolution on pointer identity change.
Transient compile errors at this line are expected during the atomic VerifyError::Legacy enum migration — all 9 arms must be updated before the crate compiles again.
Contains legacy-record discriminator (absence of all three Ed25519 sig fields) and a skew allowance to be removed in 59-04. Also the location of the `VerifyError` enum definition.

workflow: Worktree isolation is wasteful and harmful for single-plan sequential waves: adds merge/cleanup overhead with zero parallelism benefit, and forces subagents to improvise node_modules access. Use sequential mode (executor runs directly on the phase branch) when plans are strictly chained one-at-a-time.
When a worktree genuinely needs node_modules, the subagent must run `pnpm i` inside the worktree — never symlink back to the parent checkout's node_modules.

GSD failure mode #2070: executor writes SUMMARY.md but the worktree is cleaned up before the file is committed → summary lost. Mitigation: inspect the worktree after a 522 interruption; if work is complete, commit SUMMARY manually before merging.
After a 522 mid-run, inspect the worktree git log before declaring failure — the agent may have finished all substantive work and only lost the final SUMMARY commit.

`cleanup-wave` helper requires a populated `--manifest` arg; a `mktemp` template collision that produces an empty variable causes a silent no-op. Always verify the manifest variable is non-empty before invoking.
The `cleanup-wave` helper may print `commit_failed` as a false-negative even when the tracking commit lands — verify with `git log` rather than trusting the helper's exit message.
Staging DB queries are independent of in-progress local file edits and can run concurrently with a subagent mid-execution.

friction: Two Cloudflare 522 connection timeouts interrupted the session — one mid-Wave-1 executor run, one mid-merge step — requiring manual rescue of work.
`mktemp` template name collision produced an empty manifest variable, causing the `cleanup-wave` helper to silently no-op on first attempt.

Wave 1 worktree required a node_modules symlink hack by the subagent because husky pre-commit hook couldn't find lint-staged in a fresh worktree — a consequence of using worktrees unnecessarily for a sequential phase.
Nested shell quoting broke the staging `docker exec psql` invocation, requiring a fallback to stdin-piped SQL.
`cleanup-wave` tracking commit false-negative (`commit_failed` printed despite commit succeeding) required manual verification.
